# Atlas CLI — Misc Errors & Flag Parsing

Binary: `/tmp/atlas_orig` (community/unofficial dev build; `atlas version` prints
`atlas unofficial version - development`). All probes run through the normal CLI only.
Unless stated otherwise, outputs were captured piped (non-TTY), stdout and stderr
separated (`cmd >out 2>err`), and exit code via `echo $?`.

## 0. Global error conventions

- All runtime/parse errors go to **stderr** as a single line `Error: <msg>\n`
  (unless the community notice is appended — see §10). **stdout is empty** on error.
- Exit code is **1** for every error observed (flag parse errors, required-flag
  violations, connection errors, unknown commands, etc.). No other non-zero codes seen.
- **Usage text is NOT printed after errors** (cobra `SilenceUsage` behavior), except
  for the unknown-command case which appends one hint line (§5).
- Error lines end with exactly one `\n`; no leading/trailing blank lines.

## 1. Flag parsing errors (pflag/cobra verbatim)

Unknown shorthand flag:

    $ atlas schema inspect -x
    stdout: (empty)
    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: 'x' in -x
    exit: 1

Unknown long flag:

    $ atlas schema inspect --nope
    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --nope
    exit: 1

Flag missing value, long form at end of argv:

    $ atlas schema inspect --url
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
    exit: 1

Flag missing value, shorthand at end of argv (note the different quoting):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: 'u' in -u
    exit: 1

Missing value for other flags uses the same forms:

    $ atlas schema inspect --schema
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --schema
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect --env
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --env
    exit: 1

Bool flag given a non-bool value:

    $ atlas migrate apply --dry-run=x
    stderr: Error: invalid argument "x" for "--dry-run" flag: strconv.ParseBool: parsing "x": invalid syntax
    exit: 1

`--var` given without `=` (note the grammatically-off message, verbatim):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://q.db --var foo
    stderr: Error: invalid argument "foo" for "--var" flag: variables must be format as key=value, got: "foo"
    exit: 1

(`--var a=b` is accepted and has no effect on `schema inspect` output.)

## 2. `=` vs space, attached values, repeated flags

All of these are accepted and equivalent for string flags:

    atlas schema inspect --url=sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect --url sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://a.db        # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -usqlite://a.db         # attached shorthand value, exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -u=sqlite://a.db        # shorthand with '=', exit 0

Repeated flag: **last value wins** (no error, no accumulation for string flags):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://z2a.db -u sqlite://z2b.db
    exit: 0   # only z2b.db is created/inspected; z2a.db never touched

`--url` followed by another flag **consumes that flag as its value**:

    $ atlas schema inspect --url --help
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1        # i.e. url value was literally "--help"

    $ atlas schema inspect --url -h
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

A parse error later in argv **beats** `-h` (help is only honored if parsing succeeds):

    $ atlas schema inspect -h --url
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
    exit: 1        # help is NOT printed

## 3. Combined shorthands

    $ atlas schema inspect -hs foo
    exit: 0, stdout: full `schema inspect` help text (identical to --help)

`-h` inside a combined group short-circuits to help. The trailing positional `foo`
is irrelevant once help fires.

## 4. `--` terminator

Everything after `--` is positional:

    $ atlas schema inspect -- -u sqlite://x.db
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1        # -u after -- was NOT parsed as a flag

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db -- extra
    exit: 0        # "extra" silently ignored (see §7)

## 5. Unknown commands

Root level: error + suggestion block + usage hint, all on stderr:

    $ atlas schem
    stdout: (empty)
    stderr:
    Error: unknown command "schem" for "atlas"

    Did you mean this?
    	schema

    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
    exit: 1

(The suggestion entry is tab-indented. Without a near match, the
`Did you mean this?` block is omitted but `Run 'atlas --help' for usage.` remains:)

    $ atlas badcmd
    stderr:
    Error: unknown command "badcmd" for "atlas"
    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
    exit: 1

Under a **group command** (`schema`, `migrate`, `completion`), an unknown subcommand
is silently treated as a positional argument: the group's help is printed to
**stdout** and the exit code is **0** (no error at all):

    $ atlas schema badsub        # prints `atlas schema --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate badsub       # prints `atlas migrate --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate stat         # same: help, exit 0 (no "did you mean status")
    $ atlas completion badshell  # prints `atlas completion --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas schema               # bare group: same help to stdout, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate              # same, exit 0
    $ atlas                      # bare root: root help to stdout, exit 0

`atlas help <topic>` prints the same help as `<topic> --help` (byte-identical for
`help schema inspect` vs `schema inspect --help`). Unknown help topic:

    $ atlas help badcmd
    stdout:
    Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
    Usage:
      atlas [command]
    ... (root help body WITHOUT the "Manage your database schema as code"
         first line and WITHOUT the Flags section; see captured output)
    exit: 0

Exact `atlas help badcmd` stdout:

```
Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
Usage:
  atlas [command]

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  license     Display license information
  migrate     Manage versioned migration files
  schema      Work with atlas schemas.
  version     Prints this Atlas CLI version information.

Use "atlas [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

`--version` does not exist (only the `version` subcommand):

    $ atlas --version
    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --version
    exit: 1

## 6. Help flag at every position

- `-h` and `--help` are equivalent everywhere; help goes to **stdout**, exit **0**,
  stderr empty.
- `atlas -h` ≡ `atlas --help` ≡ `atlas help` ≡ bare `atlas` (root help).
- `atlas schema -h` ≡ `atlas schema --help` ≡ `atlas help schema` ≡ bare `atlas schema`.
- `atlas schema inspect -h` ≡ `--help` ≡ `atlas help schema inspect` (byte-identical).
- A `--help` placed **before** the remaining args makes everything after it irrelevant:

      $ atlas --help schema          # prints ROOT help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema --help inspect  # prints SCHEMA-group help, exit 0
      $ atlas migrate --help apply   # prints MIGRATE-group help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema inspect --help extra arg   # inspect help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema inspect extra --help       # inspect help, exit 0

- But a flag-parse error anywhere in argv overrides help (see §2, `-h --url` case).

## 7. Positional arguments / too many args

`schema inspect` accepts and **silently ignores** any number of positional args:

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db extra1 extra2
    stdout: schema "main" {\n}\n
    exit: 0

`migrate apply` takes an optional `[amount]` arg with strict validation:

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 1 2
    stderr: Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db abc
    stderr: Error: invalid amount argument "abc" (invalid syntax). Omit the argument or pass a valid integer instead
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 0
    stderr: Error: cannot apply '0' migration files
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db -1
    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: '1' in -1
    exit: 1        # negative numbers are parsed as flags

## 8. Required-flag violations

Cobra-style required flags on `schema` subcommands — plural form, quoted, comma+space
separated, in flag-declaration order:

    $ atlas schema inspect                       # no -u
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema clean
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema apply
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema apply -u sqlite://a.db        # --to missing
    stderr: Error: one of flag(s) "file" or "to" is required
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff                          # neither --from nor --to
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "from", "to" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff --from sqlite://t.db     # --to missing
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "to" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff --to sqlite://a.db       # --from missing
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "from" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate diff x
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "to", "dev-url" not set
    exit: 1

`migrate` subcommands are **inconsistent** — different code paths:

    $ atlas migrate apply            # in a dir WITHOUT ./migrations
    stderr: Error: sql/migrate: stat migrations: no such file or directory
    exit: 1        # dir check happens BEFORE the url check

    $ atlas migrate apply            # in a dir WITH ./migrations
    stderr: Error: required flag "url" not set
    exit: 1        # note SINGULAR: required flag "url" — different format
                   # from cobra's `required flag(s) "url" not set`

    $ atlas migrate status           # regardless of migrations dir
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: missing driver. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1        # empty url parsed instead of a required-flag check

    $ atlas migrate set 1            # same as status
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: missing driver. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

## 9. Invalid `-u` URLs

    $ atlas schema inspect -u ''
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect --url=
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'not a url'
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'sqlite://'
    stdout: schema "main" {\n}\n
    exit: 0        # valid! opens an empty/anonymous sqlite database

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'foo://bar/db'
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: unknown driver "foo". See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

Connection failures (exact text; host-dependent parts noted):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@localhost:3306/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp [::1]:3306: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1        # localhost resolves to ::1 here

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/db'
    stderr: Error: postgres: scanning system variables: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1        # note: postgres says "scanning", mysql says "query"

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@nonexistenthost:3306/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp: lookup nonexistenthost on 168.63.129.16:53: dial udp 168.63.129.16:53: connect: network is unreachable
    exit: 1        # the resolver IP (168.63.129.16:53) is ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT

## 10. Community-edition notices (important, stateful)

This build prints community-edition notices to **stderr**. They are rate-limited via
state files in `$HOME/.atlas/`, so they appear on the FIRST run with a fresh `$HOME`
and then go quiet. All notices respect `NO_COLOR` (see §11).

### 10a. Success-path notice (476 bytes, ends with a blank line)

Printed on successful runs of commands that connect through the schema/sqlclient
path — observed on `schema inspect` and `schema diff` (exit 0). NOT printed by
`version`, `license`, `completion *`, `--help` anywhere, `schema fmt`, `migrate status`,
`migrate apply`, `migrate validate`, `migrate new`, `migrate lint`.

Verbatim (note the trailing space after `views, ` on line 2, the tab-indented
command/URL lines, and the final blank line):

```
Notice: This Atlas edition lacks support for features such as checkpoints,
testing, down migrations, and more. Additionally, advanced database objects such as views, 
triggers, and stored procedures are not supported. To read more: https://atlasgo.io/community-edition

To install the non-community version of Atlas, use the following command:

	curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh

Or, visit the website to see all installation options:

	https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation

```

Rate limiting: on first show it writes `$HOME/.atlas/local-community.json` containing
`{"v1.us":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. The notice is suppressed until the timestamp is
more than **7 days** old (empirically: suppressed at age 600000 s, shown at 604800 s).

### 10b. Error-path notice (appended to stderr after the `Error:` line)

Fires on virtually every error path — flag parse errors, required-flag violations,
unknown root commands, connection errors, config errors, runtime errors. The error
line comes first, then the notice immediately (no blank line between):

    $ atlas schema inspect          # fresh $HOME
    stderr:
    Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    You're running the community build of Atlas, which may differ from the official version.
    If this error persists, try installing the official version as a troubleshooting step:

      curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh

    More installation options: https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
    exit: 1

(The `curl` line is indented with two spaces; the notice ends with a single `\n`,
no trailing blank line.)

Rate limiting: writes `$HOME/.atlas/community_error.json` containing
`{"last_suggested":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. Re-shown only when the timestamp is
more than **24 hours** old (suppressed at 82800 s, shown at 86400 s).

The two notices are independent (separate files); a success run does not suppress
the error notice and vice versa.

### 10c. `ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`

`ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` has **no observable effect** in this build: with a fresh
`$HOME`, both the success notice and the error notice are still printed, and the state
files are still written. (Earlier runs in a warmed `$HOME` may misleadingly suggest it
suppresses the success notice — that is the 7-day rate limit, not the env var.)

### 10d. Interplay with output

- Notices go to stderr only; stdout is byte-identical whether or not a notice fires.
- With a warmed `$HOME` (state files present and fresh), stderr is completely empty
  on success paths and contains only the `Error:` line on error paths.

## 11. TTY vs non-TTY

- Command results, help text, and `Error:` lines are identical modulo `\r\n` line
  endings added by the pty itself. No spinners or prompt differences observed on the
  probed paths (`schema inspect`, error paths, `version`).
- On a TTY the community notices are wrapped in ANSI color: `\x1b[36m` (cyan) before
  the notice text and `\x1b[0m` after it. The `Error:` line itself is NOT colored:

      Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
      ^[[36mYou're running the community build of Atlas, which may differ from the official version.
      ...
      More installation options: https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
      ^[[0m

  The success notice likewise gets `\x1b[36m` … `\x1b[0m` on a TTY.
- `NO_COLOR=1` disables the coloring (plain text, same bytes as non-TTY).

## 12. `--env` and config-file errors

`--env` (and `-c`) are persistent flags of the `schema`/`migrate` groups; they are
also accepted before the group (`atlas --env x schema inspect ...` parses fine).

`--env` with any value when no config file exists:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env nope           # cwd has no atlas.hcl
    stderr: Error: config file "atlas.hcl" was not found: stat atlas.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

Identical message/exit for `schema diff --env nope`, `schema apply --env nope`,
`migrate apply --env nope`, `migrate status --env nope`, `migrate lint --env nope`.
(`--env` is what triggers the config lookup: without `--env`, a missing default
`atlas.hcl` is silently ignored.)

With a valid `atlas.hcl` that defines envs `dev` and `prod` but not `nope`:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env nope
    stderr: Error: env "nope" not defined in config file
    exit: 1

Identical across `schema inspect`, `schema diff`, `schema apply`, `migrate status`,
`migrate apply`, `migrate lint`.

Empty `--env ''` is treated as unset:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env '' -u sqlite://e.db
    exit: 0        # normal inspect output

Explicit `-c` with a missing file errors even without `--env`:

    $ atlas schema inspect -c file://nonexistent.hcl
    stderr: Error: config file "nonexistent.hcl" was not found: stat nonexistent.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

`-c` without a URL scheme gets a helpful suggestion:

    $ atlas schema inspect -c nonexistent.hcl -u sqlite://t.db
    stderr: Error: missing scheme for config file. Did you mean file://nonexistent.hcl?
    exit: 1

Malformed config file (HCL syntax error) — format is
`<file>:<line>,<col>-<col>: <Msg>; <detail>`:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env bad    # atlas.hcl = assets/malformed_config.hcl
    stderr: Error: atlas.hcl:3,24-25: Argument or block definition required; An argument or block definition is required here.
    exit: 1

## 13. Assorted other errors

Bad Go template for `--format`:

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://fresh1.db --format '{{ bad'
    stderr: Error: parse log format: template: format:1: function "bad" not defined
    exit: 1

Missing input file for `schema fmt`:

    $ atlas schema fmt nope.hcl
    stderr: Error: stat nope.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

Schema-mismatch example (HCL declares schema "test", sqlite has "main"):

    $ atlas schema apply -u sqlite://sapx.db --to file://formatted.hcl --dev-url 'sqlite://dev?mode=memory' --auto-approve
    stderr: Error: mismatched HCL and database schemas: "main" <> "test"
    exit: 1

## 14. Captured `--help` outputs (verbatim, non-TTY, exit 0, stderr empty)

### `atlas --help`

```
Manage your database schema as code

Usage:
  atlas [command]

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  license     Display license information
  migrate     Manage versioned migration files
  schema      Work with atlas schemas.
  version     Prints this Atlas CLI version information.

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for atlas

Use "atlas [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `atlas schema --help`

```
The `atlas schema` command groups subcommands working with declarative Atlas schemas.

Usage:
  atlas schema [command]

Available Commands:
  apply       Apply an atlas schema to a target database.
  clean       Removes all objects from the connected database.
  diff        Calculate and print the diff between two schemas.
  fmt         Formats Atlas HCL files
  inspect     Inspect a database and print its schema in Atlas DDL syntax.

Flags:
  -c, --config string        select config (project) file using URL format (default "file://atlas.hcl")
      --env string           set which env from the config file to use
  -h, --help                 help for schema
      --var <name>=<value>   input variables (default [])

Use "atlas schema [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `atlas migrate --help`

```
'atlas migrate' wraps several sub-commands for migration management.

Usage:
  atlas migrate [command]

Available Commands:
  apply       Applies pending migration files on the connected database.
  diff        Compute the diff between the migration directory and a desired state and create a new migration file.
  hash        Hash (re-)creates an integrity hash file for the migration directory.
  import      Import a migration directory from another migration management tool to the Atlas format.
  lint        Run analysis on the migration directory
  new         Creates a new empty migration file in the migration directory.
  set         Set the current version of the migration history table.
  status      Get information about the current migration status.
  validate    Validates the migration directories checksum and SQL statements.

Flags:
  -c, --config string        select config (project) file using URL format (default "file://atlas.hcl")
      --env string           set which env from the config file to use
  -h, --help                 help for migrate
      --var <name>=<value>   input variables (default [])

Use "atlas migrate [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `atlas schema inspect --help`

```
'atlas schema inspect' connects to the given database and inspects its schema.
It then prints to the screen the schema of that database in Atlas DDL syntax. This output can be
saved to a file, commonly by redirecting the output to a file named with a ".hcl" suffix:

  atlas schema inspect -u "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/dbname" > schema.hcl

This file can then be edited and used with the `atlas schema apply` command to plan
and execute schema migrations against the given database. In cases where users wish to inspect
all multiple schemas in a given database (for instance a MySQL server may contain multiple named
databases), omit the relevant part from the url, e.g. "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/".
To select specific schemas from the databases, users may use the "--schema" (or "-s" shorthand)
flag.

Usage:
  atlas schema inspect [flags]

Examples:
  atlas schema inspect -u "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/dbname"
  atlas schema inspect -u "mariadb://user:pass@localhost:3306/" --schema=schemaA,schemaB -s schemaC
  atlas schema inspect --url "postgres://user:pass@host:port/dbname?sslmode=disable"
  atlas schema inspect -u "sqlite://file:ex1.db?_fk=1"

Flags:
  -u, --url string        [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a resource using the URL format
      --dev-url string    [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a dev database using the URL format
  -s, --schema strings    set schema names
      --exclude strings   list of glob patterns used to filter resources from applying
      --format string     Go template to use to format the output
  -h, --help              help for inspect

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string        select config (project) file using URL format (default "file://atlas.hcl")
      --env string           set which env from the config file to use
      --var <name>=<value>   input variables (default [])
```

### `atlas schema diff --help`

```
'atlas schema diff' reads the state of two given schema definitions, 
calculates the difference in their schemas, and prints a plan of
SQL statements to migrate the "from" database to the schema of the "to" database.
The database states can be read from a connected database, an HCL project or a migration directory.

Usage:
  atlas schema diff [flags]

Examples:
  atlas schema diff --from "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/test" --to "file://schema.hcl"
  atlas schema diff --from "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306" --to "file://schema_1.hcl" --to "file://schema_2.hcl"
  atlas schema diff --from "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306" --to "file://migrations" --format '{{ sql . "  " }}'

Flags:
  -f, --from strings      [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a resource using the URL format
      --to strings        [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a desired state using the URL format
      --dev-url string    [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a dev database using the URL format
  -s, --schema strings    set schema names
      --exclude strings   list of glob patterns used to filter resources from applying
      --include strings   list of glob patterns used to select which resources to keep in inspection
      --format string     Go template to use to format the output

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string        select config (project) file using URL format (default "file://atlas.hcl")
      --env string           set which env from the config file to use
      --var <name>=<value>   input variables (default [])
```

(Note: the first line of `schema diff` help ends with a trailing space after `definitions, `.)

### `atlas migrate apply --help`

```
'atlas migrate apply' reads the migration state of the connected database and computes what migrations are pending.
It then attempts to apply the pending migration files in the correct order onto the database. 
The first argument denotes the maximum number of migration files to apply.
As a safety measure 'atlas migrate apply' will abort with an error, if:
  - the migration directory is not in sync with the 'atlas.sum' file
  - the migration and database history do not match each other

If run with the "--dry-run" flag, atlas will not execute any SQL.

Usage:
  atlas migrate apply [flags] [amount]

Examples:
  atlas migrate apply -u "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/dbname"
  atlas migrate apply --dir "file:///path/to/migration/directory" --url "mysql://user:pass@localhost:3306/dbname" 1
  atlas migrate apply --env dev 1
  atlas migrate apply --dry-run --env dev 1

Flags:
  -u, --url string                [driver://username:password@address/dbname?param=value] select a resource using the URL format
      --dir string                select migration directory using URL format (default "file://migrations")
      --format string             Go template to use to format the output
      --revisions-schema string   name of the schema the revisions table resides in
      --dry-run                   print SQL without executing it
      --lock-timeout duration     set how long to wait for the database lock (default 10s)
      --baseline string           start the first migration after the given baseline version
      --tx-mode string            set transaction mode [none, file, all] (default "file")
      --exec-order string         set file execution order [linear, linear-skip, non-linear] (default "linear")
      --allow-dirty               allow start working on a non-clean database
  -h, --help                      help for apply

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string        select config (project) file using URL format (default "file://atlas.hcl")
      --env string           set which env from the config file to use
      --var <name>=<value>   input variables (default [])
```

(Note: line 2 of `migrate apply` help ends with a trailing space after `database. `.)

# Atlas CLI — Misc Errors & Flag Parsing

Binary: `/tmp/atlas_orig` (community/unofficial dev build; `atlas version` prints
`atlas unofficial version - development`). All probes run through the normal CLI only.
Unless stated otherwise, outputs were captured piped (non-TTY), stdout and stderr
separated (`cmd >out 2>err`), and exit code via `echo $?`.

## 0. Global error conventions

- All runtime/parse errors go to **stderr** as a single line `Error: <msg>\n`
  (unless the community notice is appended — see §10). **stdout is empty** on error.
- Exit code is **1** for every error observed (flag parse errors, required-flag
  violations, connection errors, unknown commands, etc.). No other non-zero codes seen.
- **Usage text is NOT printed after errors** (cobra `SilenceUsage` behavior), except
  for the unknown-command case which appends one hint line (§5).
- Error lines end with exactly one `\n`; no leading/trailing blank lines.

## 1. Flag parsing errors (pflag/cobra verbatim)

Unknown shorthand flag:

    $ atlas schema inspect -x
    stdout: (empty)
    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: 'x' in -x
    exit: 1

Unknown long flag:

    $ atlas schema inspect --nope
    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --nope
    exit: 1

Flag missing value, long form at end of argv:

    $ atlas schema inspect --url
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
    exit: 1

Flag missing value, shorthand at end of argv (note the different quoting):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: 'u' in -u
    exit: 1

Missing value for other flags uses the same forms:

    $ atlas schema inspect --schema
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --schema
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect --env
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --env
    exit: 1

Bool flag given a non-bool value:

    $ atlas migrate apply --dry-run=x
    stderr: Error: invalid argument "x" for "--dry-run" flag: strconv.ParseBool: parsing "x": invalid syntax
    exit: 1

`--var` given without `=` (note the grammatically-off message, verbatim):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://q.db --var foo
    stderr: Error: invalid argument "foo" for "--var" flag: variables must be format as key=value, got: "foo"
    exit: 1

(`--var a=b` is accepted and has no effect on `schema inspect` output.)

## 2. `=` vs space, attached values, repeated flags

All of these are accepted and equivalent for string flags:

    atlas schema inspect --url=sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect --url sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://a.db        # exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -usqlite://a.db         # attached shorthand value, exit 0
    atlas schema inspect -u=sqlite://a.db        # shorthand with '=', exit 0

Repeated flag: **last value wins** (no error, no accumulation for string flags):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://z2a.db -u sqlite://z2b.db
    exit: 0   # only z2b.db is created/inspected; z2a.db never touched

`--url` followed by another flag **consumes that flag as its value**:

    $ atlas schema inspect --url --help
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1        # i.e. url value was literally "--help"

    $ atlas schema inspect --url -h
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

A parse error later in argv **beats** `-h` (help is only honored if parsing succeeds):

    $ atlas schema inspect -h --url
    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
    exit: 1        # help is NOT printed

## 3. Combined shorthands

    $ atlas schema inspect -hs foo
    exit: 0, stdout: full `schema inspect` help text (identical to --help)

`-h` inside a combined group short-circuits to help. The trailing positional `foo`
is irrelevant once help fires.

## 4. `--` terminator

Everything after `--` is positional:

    $ atlas schema inspect -- -u sqlite://x.db
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1        # -u after -- was NOT parsed as a flag

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db -- extra
    exit: 0        # "extra" silently ignored (see §7)

## 5. Unknown commands

Root level: error + suggestion block + usage hint, all on stderr:

    $ atlas schem
    stdout: (empty)
    stderr:
    Error: unknown command "schem" for "atlas"

    Did you mean this?
    	schema

    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
    exit: 1

(The suggestion entry is tab-indented. Without a near match, the
`Did you mean this?` block is omitted but `Run 'atlas --help' for usage.` remains:)

    $ atlas badcmd
    stderr:
    Error: unknown command "badcmd" for "atlas"
    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
    exit: 1

Under a **group command** (`schema`, `migrate`, `completion`), an unknown subcommand
is silently treated as a positional argument: the group's help is printed to
**stdout** and the exit code is **0** (no error at all):

    $ atlas schema badsub        # prints `atlas schema --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate badsub       # prints `atlas migrate --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate stat         # same: help, exit 0 (no "did you mean status")
    $ atlas completion badshell  # prints `atlas completion --help` text, exit 0
    $ atlas schema               # bare group: same help to stdout, exit 0
    $ atlas migrate              # same, exit 0
    $ atlas                      # bare root: root help to stdout, exit 0

`atlas help <topic>` prints the same help as `<topic> --help` (byte-identical for
`help schema inspect` vs `schema inspect --help`). Unknown help topic:

    $ atlas help badcmd
    stdout:
    Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
    Usage:
      atlas [command]
    ... (root help body WITHOUT the "Manage your database schema as code"
         first line and WITHOUT the Flags section; see captured output)
    exit: 0

Exact `atlas help badcmd` stdout:

```
Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
Usage:
  atlas [command]

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  license     Display license information
  migrate     Manage versioned migration files
  schema      Work with atlas schemas.
  version     Prints this Atlas CLI version information.

Use "atlas [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

`--version` does not exist (only the `version` subcommand):

    $ atlas --version
    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --version
    exit: 1

## 6. Help flag at every position

- `-h` and `--help` are equivalent everywhere; help goes to **stdout**, exit **0**,
  stderr empty.
- `atlas -h` ≡ `atlas --help` ≡ `atlas help` ≡ bare `atlas` (root help).
- `atlas schema -h` ≡ `atlas schema --help` ≡ `atlas help schema` ≡ bare `atlas schema`.
- `atlas schema inspect -h` ≡ `--help` ≡ `atlas help schema inspect` (byte-identical).
- A `--help` placed **before** the remaining args makes everything after it irrelevant:

      $ atlas --help schema          # prints ROOT help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema --help inspect  # prints SCHEMA-group help, exit 0
      $ atlas migrate --help apply   # prints MIGRATE-group help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema inspect --help extra arg   # inspect help, exit 0
      $ atlas schema inspect extra --help       # inspect help, exit 0

- But a flag-parse error anywhere in argv overrides help (see §2, `-h --url` case).

## 7. Positional arguments / too many args

`schema inspect` accepts and **silently ignores** any number of positional args:

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db extra1 extra2
    stdout: schema "main" {\n}\n
    exit: 0

`migrate apply` takes an optional `[amount]` arg with strict validation:

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 1 2
    stderr: Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db abc
    stderr: Error: invalid amount argument "abc" (invalid syntax). Omit the argument or pass a valid integer instead
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 0
    stderr: Error: cannot apply '0' migration files
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db -1
    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: '1' in -1
    exit: 1        # negative numbers are parsed as flags

## 8. Required-flag violations

Cobra-style required flags on `schema` subcommands — plural form, quoted, comma+space
separated, in flag-declaration order:

    $ atlas schema inspect                       # no -u
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema clean
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema apply
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema apply -u sqlite://a.db        # --to missing
    stderr: Error: one of flag(s) "file" or "to" is required
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff                          # neither --from nor --to
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "from", "to" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff --from sqlite://t.db     # --to missing
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "to" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema diff --to sqlite://a.db       # --from missing
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "from" not set
    exit: 1

    $ atlas migrate diff x
    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "to", "dev-url" not set
    exit: 1

`migrate` subcommands are **inconsistent** — different code paths:

    $ atlas migrate apply            # in a dir WITHOUT ./migrations
    stderr: Error: sql/migrate: stat migrations: no such file or directory
    exit: 1        # dir check happens BEFORE the url check

    $ atlas migrate apply            # in a dir WITH ./migrations
    stderr: Error: required flag "url" not set
    exit: 1        # note SINGULAR: required flag "url" — different format
                   # from cobra's `required flag(s) "url" not set`

    $ atlas migrate status           # regardless of migrations dir
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: missing driver. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1        # empty url parsed instead of a required-flag check

    $ atlas migrate set 1            # same as status
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: missing driver. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

## 9. Invalid `-u` URLs

    $ atlas schema inspect -u ''
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect --url=
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'not a url'
    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'sqlite://'
    stdout: schema "main" {\n}\n
    exit: 0        # valid! opens an empty/anonymous sqlite database

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'foo://bar/db'
    stderr: Error: sql/sqlclient: unknown driver "foo". See: https://atlasgo.io/url
    exit: 1

Connection failures (exact text; host-dependent parts noted):

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@localhost:3306/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp [::1]:3306: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1        # localhost resolves to ::1 here

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:1/db'
    stderr: Error: postgres: scanning system variables: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
    exit: 1        # note: postgres says "scanning", mysql says "query"

    $ atlas schema inspect -u 'mysql://u:p@nonexistenthost:3306/db'
    stderr: Error: mysql: query system variables: dial tcp: lookup nonexistenthost on 168.63.129.16:53: dial udp 168.63.129.16:53: connect: network is unreachable
    exit: 1        # the resolver IP (168.63.129.16:53) is ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT

## 10. Community-edition notices (important, stateful)

This build prints community-edition notices to **stderr**. They are rate-limited via
state files in `$HOME/.atlas/`, so they appear on the FIRST run with a fresh `$HOME`
and then go quiet. All notices respect `NO_COLOR` (see §11).

### 10a. Success-path notice (476 bytes, ends with a blank line)

Printed on successful runs of commands that connect through the schema/sqlclient
path — observed on `schema inspect` and `schema diff` (exit 0). NOT printed by
`version`, `license`, `completion *`, `--help` anywhere, `schema fmt`, `migrate status`,
`migrate apply`, `migrate validate`, `migrate new`, `migrate lint`.

Verbatim (note the trailing space after `views, ` on line 2, the tab-indented
command/URL lines, and the final blank line):

```
Notice: This Atlas edition lacks support for features such as checkpoints,
testing, down migrations, and more. Additionally, advanced database objects such as views, 
triggers, and stored procedures are not supported. To read more: https://atlasgo.io/community-edition

To install the non-community version of Atlas, use the following command:

	curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh

Or, visit the website to see all installation options:

	https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation

```

Rate limiting: on first show it writes `$HOME/.atlas/local-community.json` containing
`{"v1.us":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. The notice is suppressed until the timestamp is
more than **7 days** old (empirically: suppressed at age 600000 s, shown at 604800 s).

### 10b. Error-path notice (appended to stderr after the `Error:` line)

Fires on virtually every error path — flag parse errors, required-flag violations,
unknown root commands, connection errors, config errors, runtime errors. The error
line comes first, then the notice immediately (no blank line between):

    $ atlas schema inspect          # fresh $HOME
    stderr:
    Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
    You're running the community build of Atlas, which may differ from the official version.
    If this error persists, try installing the official version as a troubleshooting step:

      curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh

    More installation options: https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
    exit: 1

(The `curl` line is indented with two spaces; the notice ends with a single `\n`,
no trailing blank line.)

Rate limiting: writes `$HOME/.atlas/community_error.json` containing
`{"last_suggested":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. Re-shown only when the timestamp is
more than **24 hours** old (suppressed at 82800 s, shown at 86400 s).

The two notices are independent (separate files); a success run does not suppress
the error notice and vice versa.

### 10c. `ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`

`ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` has **no observable effect** in this build: with a fresh
`$HOME`, both the success notice and the error notice are still printed, and the state
files are still written. (Earlier runs in a warmed `$HOME` may misleadingly suggest it
suppresses the success notice — that is the 7-day rate limit, not the env var.)

### 10d. Interplay with output

- Notices go to stderr only; stdout is byte-identical whether or not a notice fires.
- With a warmed `$HOME` (state files present and fresh), stderr is completely empty
  on success paths and contains only the `Error:` line on error paths.

## 11. TTY vs non-TTY

- Command results, help text, and `Error:` lines are identical modulo `\r\n` line
  endings added by the pty itself. No spinners or prompt differences observed on the
  probed paths (`schema inspect`, error paths, `version`).
- On a TTY the community notices are wrapped in ANSI color: `\x1b[36m` (cyan) before
  the notice text and `\x1b[0m` after it. The `Error:` line itself is NOT colored:

      Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
      ^[[36mYou're running the community build of Atlas, which may differ from the official version.
      ...
      More installation options: https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
      ^[[0m

  The success notice likewise gets `\x1b[36m` … `\x1b[0m` on a TTY.
- `NO_COLOR=1` disables the coloring (plain text, same bytes as non-TTY).

## 12. `--env` and config-file errors

`--env` (and `-c`) are persistent flags of the `schema`/`migrate` groups; they are
also accepted before the group (`atlas --env x schema inspect ...` parses fine).

`--env` with any value when no config file exists:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env nope           # cwd has no atlas.hcl
    stderr: Error: config file "atlas.hcl" was not found: stat atlas.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

Identical message/exit for `schema diff --env nope`, `schema apply --env nope`,
`migrate apply --env nope`, `migrate status --env nope`, `migrate lint --env nope`.
(`--env` is what triggers the config lookup: without `--env`, a missing default
`atlas.hcl` is silently ignored.)

With a valid `atlas.hcl` that defines envs `dev` and `prod` but not `nope`:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env nope
    stderr: Error: env "nope" not defined in config file
    exit: 1

Identical across `schema inspect`, `schema diff`, `schema apply`, `migrate status`,
`migrate apply`, `migrate lint`.

Empty `--env ''` is treated as unset:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env '' -u sqlite://e.db
    exit: 0        # normal inspect output

Explicit `-c` with a missing file errors even without `--env`:

    $ atlas schema inspect -c file://nonexistent.hcl
    stderr: Error: config file "nonexistent.hcl" was not found: stat nonexistent.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

`-c` without a URL scheme gets a helpful suggestion:

    $ atlas schema inspect -c nonexistent.hcl -u sqlite://t.db
    stderr: Error: missing scheme for config file. Did you mean file://nonexistent.hcl?
    exit: 1

Malformed config file (HCL syntax error) — format is
`<file>:<line>,<col>-<col>: <Msg>; <detail>`:

    $ atlas schema inspect --env bad    # atlas.hcl = assets/malformed_config.hcl
    stderr: Error: atlas.hcl:3,24-25: Argument or block definition required; An argument or block definition is required here.
    exit: 1

## 13. Assorted other errors

Bad Go template for `--format`:

    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://fresh1.db --format '{{ bad'
    stderr: Error: parse log format: template: format:1: function "bad" not defined
    exit: 1

Missing input file for `schema fmt`:

    $ atlas schema fmt nope.hcl
    stderr: Error: stat nope.hcl: no such file or directory
    exit: 1

Schema-mismatch example (HCL declares schema "test", sqlite has "main"):

    $ atlas schema apply -u sqlite://sapx.db --to file://formatted.hcl --dev-url 'sqlite://dev?mode=memory' --auto-approve
    stderr: Error: mismatched HCL and database schemas: "main" <> "test"
    exit: 1

## 14. Captured `--help` outputs (verbatim, non-TTY, exit 0, stderr empty)

```

  version     Prints this Atlas CLI version information.

Flags:

Use "atlas [command] --help" for more information about a command.

```

```
Usage:

Use "atlas schema [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `atlas schema inspect --help`

```
'atlas schema inspect' connects to the given database and inspects its schema.
It then prints to the screen the schema of that database in Atlas DDL syntax. This output can be
saved to a file, commonly by redirecting the output to a file named with a ".hcl" suffix:
```

Spec written to `/workspace/specs/migrate_dir.md`. Five key findings:

1. **atlas.sum is a chained hash, not per-file**: one running SHA-256 over sorted `*.sql` files (byte-wise name order) — for each file, name bytes then raw content bytes are fed in, and the file's listed hash is the *cumulative* digest (`h1:` + std base64). Adding a file at the front rewrites every later file's hash. A Python reference implementation in the spec reproduces the binary's `atlas.sum` byte-for-byte on 8 test dirs.
2. **Total line** = `h1:` + base64(sha256 of concatenated `name + base64-per-file-hash-string` per file, same order); empty dir yields `h1:47DEQpj8...SuFU=` (sha256 of empty string) + `\n`. Only lowercase `.sql` regular files in the top level count (hidden `.foo.sql` included, `.SQL`/subdirs/non-sql excluded).
3. **`migrate new`** writes an empty `<localtime YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>[_name].sql` (0644), auto-creates the missing dir, re-writes `atlas.sum`, prints nothing on success — but *validates the existing sum first* and aborts with the checksum report on mismatch. `--dir` requires a URL scheme (`Error: missing scheme for dir url. Did you mean "file://migrations"? ` — trailing space is exact).
4. **`migrate validate`** is silent exit-0 when OK; on mismatch it prints a human report to **stdout** (`You have a checksum error...` + `\tL<n>: <file> was edited|removed|added`, L = 1-based atlas.sum line, only first discrepancy shown) and `Error: checksum mismatch` to **stderr**, exit 1; missing sum says `Error: checksum file not found`; corrupt format says `Error: checksum file format invalid`. `hash`/`validate` silently ignore extra positional args; `new` errors with `accepts at most 1 arg(s)`.
5. **No TTY-dependent behavior** (no colors/prompts/spinners; pty only adds `\r`). `--dir-format` changes naming/templates: golang-migrate makes `<ts>_<name>.up.sql`+`.down.sql`, flyway makes `V<ts>__<name>.sql`+`U...`, goose/dbmate/liquibase pre-fill annotation comments — and only up/V files enter `atlas.sum`.

Spec written to `/workspace/specs/errors_misc.md`. Five-line summary of the most important findings:

1. **Community notices are stateful and rate-limited**: a 476-byte "Notice: This Atlas edition lacks support..." goes to stderr on successful `schema inspect`/`diff` (once per 7 days, tracked in `~/.atlas/local-community.json`), and every error path appends "You're running the community build of Atlas..." after the `Error:` line (once per 24h, tracked in `~/.atlas/community_error.json`). `ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` has **no effect** on either; on TTY they're wrapped in `\x1b[36m`/`\x1b[0m`, disabled by `NO_COLOR`.
2. **Error format is uniform**: `Error: <msg>` on stderr only, exit 1, no usage printed — except unknown root commands which add `Did you mean this?` suggestions and `Run 'atlas --help' for usage.`
3. **Unknown subcommands under group commands are not errors**: `atlas schema badsub` / `migrate badsub` / `completion badshell` print the group help to stdout and exit 0.
4. **Required-flag messages are inconsistent**: schema commands use cobra's plural `required flag(s) "url" not set`, but `migrate apply` (with migrations dir present) says singular `required flag "url" not set`, and `migrate status`/`set` skip the check entirely, failing with `sql/sqlclient: missing driver`.
5. **pflag quirks confirmed verbatim**: `--url` consumes a following `--help`/`-h` as its value; a parse error anywhere beats `-h`; `-u ''`/`not a url` → `missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url`; `sqlite://` (bare) is valid; positional args to `schema inspect` are silently ignored while `migrate apply` strictly validates its `[amount]` arg (`accepts at most 1 arg(s)`, `invalid amount argument "abc" (invalid syntax). Omit the argument or pass a valid integer instead`, `cannot apply '0' migration files`).

Five most important findings:

297	- `atlas migrate aapply` → full `migrate` help, exit `0`.
298	- `atlas completion badshell` → full `completion` help, exit `0` (see below).
299	- `atlas completion badshell extra` → same, exit `0`.
300	- `atlas completion Bash` → full `completion` help, exit `0` (case-sensitive: `Bash` is not `bash`).

473	### Generated scripts
474	
475	Each of `atlas completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` exits `0`, writes the script to stdout (stderr empty), ends with a trailing `\n`. Sizes: bash 11710 bytes / 338 lines, zsh 7712 bytes / 212 lines, fish 9601 bytes / 235 lines, powershell 9794 bytes / 245 lines. Raw copies are saved alongside this spec as `completion_bash.txt`, `completion_zsh.txt`, `completion_fish.txt`, `completion_powershell.txt`.
476	
477	Each command also accepts `--no-descriptions` (exit `0`), which changes exactly one line in the generated script — the hidden completion command switches from `__complete` to `__completeNoDesc`:
478	
479	- bash line 26: `requestComp="${words[0]} __complete ${args[*]}"` → `requestComp="${words[0]} __completeNoDesc ${args[*]}"`
480	- zsh line 49: `requestComp="${words[1]} __complete ${words[2,-1]}"` → `requestComp="${words[1]} __completeNoDesc ${words[2,-1]}"`
481	- fish line 22: `set -l requestComp "ATLAS_ACTIVE_HELP=0 $args[1] __complete $args[2..-1] $lastArg"` → `... __completeNoDesc ...`
482	- powershell line 49: `$RequestComp="$Program __complete $Arguments"` → `$RequestComp="$Program __completeNoDesc $Arguments"`

697	__atlas_handle_standard_completion_case() {
698	    local tab=$'\t' comp
699	
700	    # Short circuit to optimize if we don't have descriptions
701	    if [[ "${completions[*]}" != *$tab* ]]; then
702	        IFS=$'\n' read -ra COMPREPLY -d '' < <(compgen -W "${completions[*]}" -- "$cur")
703	        return 0
704	    fi
705	
706	    local longest=0
707	    local compline
708	    # Look for the longest completion so that we can format things nicely
709	    while IFS='' read -r compline; do
710	        [[ -z $compline ]] && continue
711	        # Strip any description before checking the length
712	        comp=${compline%%$tab*}
713	        # Only consider the completions that match
714	        [[ $comp == "$cur"* ]] || continue
715	        COMPREPLY+=("$compline")
716	        if ((${#comp}>longest)); then
717	            longest=${#comp}
718	        fi
719	    done < <(printf "%s\n" "${completions[@]}")

721	    # If there is a single completion left, remove the description text
722	    if ((${#COMPREPLY[*]} == 1)); then
723	        __atlas_debug "COMPREPLY[0]: ${COMPREPLY[0]}"
724	        comp="${COMPREPLY[0]%%$tab*}"
725	        __atlas_debug "Removed description from single completion, which is now: ${comp}"
726	        COMPREPLY[0]=$comp
727	    else # Format the descriptions
728	        __atlas_format_comp_descriptions $longest

745	__atlas_format_comp_descriptions()
746	{
747	    local tab=$'\t'
748	    local comp desc maxdesclength
749	    local longest=$1
750	
751	    local i ci
752	    for ci in ${!COMPREPLY[*]}; do
753	        comp=${COMPREPLY[ci]}
754	        # Properly format the description string which follows a tab character if there is one
755	        if [[ "$comp" == *$tab* ]]; then
756	            __atlas_debug "Original comp: $comp"
757	            desc=${comp#*$tab}
758	            comp=${comp%%$tab*}
759	
760	            # $COLUMNS stores the current shell width.
761	            # Remove an extra 4 because we add 2 spaces and 2 parentheses.
762	            maxdesclength=$(( COLUMNS - longest - 4 ))
763	
764	            # Make sure we can fit a description of at least 8 characters
765	            # if we are to align the descriptions.
766	            if ((maxdesclength > 8)); then
767	                # Add the proper number of spaces to align the descriptions
768	                for ((i = ${#comp} ; i < longest ; i++)); do
769	                    comp+=" "
770	                done
771	            else
772	                # Don't pad the descriptions so we can fit more text after the completion
773	                maxdesclength=$(( COLUMNS - ${#comp} - 4 ))
774	            fi
775	
776	            # If there is enough space for any description text,
777	            # truncate the descriptions that are too long for the shell width
778	            if ((maxdesclength > 0)); then
779	                if ((${#desc} > maxdesclength)); then
780	                    desc=${desc:0:$(( maxdesclength - 1 ))}
781	                    desc+="…"
782	                fi
783	                comp+="  ($desc)"
784	            fi
785	            COMPREPLY[ci]=$comp
786	            __atlas_debug "Final comp: $comp"
787	        fi
788	    done
789	}

814

816	    __atlas_get_completion_results
817	    __atlas_process_completion_results
818	}
819	
820	if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
821	    complete -o default -F __start_atlas atlas
822	else
823	    complete -o default -o nospace -F __start_atlas atlas
824	fi

1	# Atlas CLI — Misc Errors & Flag Parsing
2	
3	Binary: `/tmp/atlas_orig` (community/unofficial dev build; `atlas version` prints
4	`atlas unofficial version - development`). All probes run through the normal CLI only.
5	Unless stated otherwise, outputs were captured piped (non-TTY), stdout and stderr
6	separated (`cmd >out 2>err`), and exit code via `echo $?`.
7	
8	## 0. Global error conventions
9	
10	- All runtime/parse errors go to **stderr** as a single line `Error: <msg>\n`
11	  (unless the community notice is appended — see §10). **stdout is empty** on error.
12	- Exit code is **1** for every error observed (flag parse errors, required-flag
13	  violations, connection errors, unknown commands, etc.). No other non-zero codes seen.
14	- **Usage text is NOT printed after errors** (cobra `SilenceUsage` behavior), except
15	  for the unknown-command case which appends one hint line (§5).
16	- Error lines end with exactly one `\n`; no leading/trailing blank lines.
17	
18	## 1. Flag parsing errors (pflag/cobra verbatim)
19	
20	Unknown shorthand flag:
21	
22	    $ atlas schema inspect -x
23	    stdout: (empty)
24	    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: 'x' in -x
25	    exit: 1
26	
27	Unknown long flag:
28	
29	    $ atlas schema inspect --nope
30	    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --nope
31	    exit: 1
32	
33	Flag missing value, long form at end of argv:
34	
35	    $ atlas schema inspect --url
36	    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
37	    exit: 1
38	
39	Flag missing value, shorthand at end of argv (note the different quoting):
40	
41	    $ atlas schema inspect -u
42	    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: 'u' in -u
43	    exit: 1
44	
45	Missing value for other flags uses the same forms:
46	
47	    $ atlas schema inspect --schema
48	    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --schema
49	    exit: 1
50	
51	    $ atlas schema inspect --env
52	    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --env
53	    exit: 1
54	
55	Bool flag given a non-bool value:
56	
57	    $ atlas migrate apply --dry-run=x
58	    stderr: Error: invalid argument "x" for "--dry-run" flag: strconv.ParseBool: parsing "x": invalid syntax
59	    exit: 1
60	
61	`--var` given without `=` (note the grammatically-off message, verbatim):
62	
63	    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://q.db --var foo
64	    stderr: Error: invalid argument "foo" for "--var" flag: variables must be format as key=value, got: "foo"
65	    exit: 1
66	
67	(`--var a=b` is accepted and has no effect on `schema inspect` output.)
68	
69	## 2. `=` vs space, attached values, repeated flags
70	
71	All of these are accepted and equivalent for string flags:
72	
73	    atlas schema inspect --url=sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
74	    atlas schema inspect --url sqlite://a.db     # exit 0
75	    atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://a.db        # exit 0
76	    atlas schema inspect -usqlite://a.db         # attached shorthand value, exit 0
77	    atlas schema inspect -u=sqlite://a.db        # shorthand with '=', exit 0
78	
79	Repeated flag: **last value wins** (no error, no accumulation for string flags):
80	
81	    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://z2a.db -u sqlite://z2b.db
82	    exit: 0   # only z2b.db is created/inspected; z2a.db never touched
83	
84	`--url` followed by another flag **consumes that flag as its value**:
85	
86	    $ atlas schema inspect --url --help
87	    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
88	    exit: 1        # i.e. url value was literally "--help"
89	
90	    $ atlas schema inspect --url -h
91	    stderr: Error: missing scheme. See: https://atlasgo.io/url
92	    exit: 1
93	
94	A parse error later in argv **beats** `-h` (help is only honored if parsing succeeds):
95	
96	    $ atlas schema inspect -h --url
97	    stderr: Error: flag needs an argument: --url
98	    exit: 1        # help is NOT printed
99	
100	## 3. Combined shorthands
101	
102	    $ atlas schema inspect -hs foo
103	    exit: 0, stdout: full `schema inspect` help text (identical to --help)
104	
105	`-h` inside a combined group short-circuits to help. The trailing positional `foo`
106	is irrelevant once help fires.
107	
108	## 4. `--` terminator
109	
110	Everything after `--` is positional:
111	
112	    $ atlas schema inspect -- -u sqlite://x.db
113	    stderr: Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
114	    exit: 1        # -u after -- was NOT parsed as a flag
115	
116	    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db -- extra
117	    exit: 0        # "extra" silently ignored (see §7)
118	
119	## 5. Unknown commands
120	
121	Root level: error + suggestion block + usage hint, all on stderr:
122	
123	    $ atlas schem
124	    stdout: (empty)
125	    stderr:
126	    Error: unknown command "schem" for "atlas"
127	
128	    Did you mean this?
129	    	schema
130	
131	    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
132	    exit: 1
133	
134	(The suggestion entry is tab-indented. Without a near match, the
135	`Did you mean this?` block is omitted but `Run 'atlas --help' for usage.` remains:)
136	
137	    $ atlas badcmd
138	    stderr:
139	    Error: unknown command "badcmd" for "atlas"
140	    Run 'atlas --help' for usage.
141	    exit: 1
142	
143	Under a **group command** (`schema`, `migrate`, `completion`), an unknown subcommand
144	is silently treated as a positional argument: the group's help is printed to
145	**stdout** and the exit code is **0** (no error at all):
146	
147	    $ atlas schema badsub        # prints `atlas schema --help` text, exit 0
148	    $ atlas migrate badsub       # prints `atlas migrate --help` text, exit 0
149	    $ atlas migrate stat         # same: help, exit 0 (no "did you mean status")
150	    $ atlas completion badshell  # prints `atlas completion --help` text, exit 0
151	    $ atlas schema               # bare group: same help to stdout, exit 0
152	    $ atlas migrate              # same, exit 0
153	    $ atlas                      # bare root: root help to stdout, exit 0
154	
155	`atlas help <topic>` prints the same help as `<topic> --help` (byte-identical for
156	`help schema inspect` vs `schema inspect --help`). Unknown help topic:
157	
158	    $ atlas help badcmd
159	    stdout:
160	    Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
161	    Usage:
162	      atlas [command]
163	    ... (root help body WITHOUT the "Manage your database schema as code"
164	         first line and WITHOUT the Flags section; see captured output)
165	    exit: 0
166	
167	Exact `atlas help badcmd` stdout:
168	
169	```
170	Unknown help topic [`badcmd`]
171	Usage:
172	  atlas [command]
173	
174	Available Commands:
175	  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
176	  help        Help about any command
177	  license     Display license information
178	  migrate     Manage versioned migration files
179	  schema      Work with atlas schemas.
180	  version     Prints this Atlas CLI version information.
181	
182	Use "atlas [command] --help" for more information about a command.
183	```

185	`--version` does not exist (only the `version` subcommand):
186	
187	    $ atlas --version
188	    stderr: Error: unknown flag: --version
189	    exit: 1

191	## 6. Help flag at every position
192	
193	- `-h` and `--help` are equivalent everywhere; help goes to **stdout**, exit **0**,
194	  stderr empty.
195	- `atlas -h` ≡ `atlas --help` ≡ `atlas help` ≡ bare `atlas` (root help).
196	- `atlas schema -h` ≡ `atlas schema --help` ≡ `atlas help schema` ≡ bare `atlas schema`.
197	- `atlas schema inspect -h` ≡ `--help` ≡ `atlas help schema inspect` (byte-identical).
198	- A `--help` placed **before** the remaining args makes everything after it irrelevant:
199	
200	      $ atlas --help schema          # prints ROOT help, exit 0
201	      $ atlas schema --help inspect  # prints SCHEMA-group help, exit 0
202	      $ atlas migrate --help apply   # prints MIGRATE-group help, exit 0
203	      $ atlas schema inspect --help extra arg   # inspect help, exit 0
204	      $ atlas schema inspect extra --help       # inspect help, exit 0
205	
206	- But a flag-parse error anywhere in argv overrides help (see §2, `-h --url` case).
207	
208	## 7. Positional arguments / too many args
209	
210	`schema inspect` accepts and **silently ignores** any number of positional args:
211	
212	    $ atlas schema inspect -u sqlite://t.db extra1 extra2
213	    stdout: schema "main" {\n}\n
214	    exit: 0
215	
216	`migrate apply` takes an optional `[amount]` arg with strict validation:
217	
218	    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 1 2
219	    stderr: Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
220	    exit: 1
221	
222	    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db abc
223	    stderr: Error: invalid amount argument "abc" (invalid syntax). Omit the argument or pass a valid integer instead
224	    exit: 1
225	
226	    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db 0
227	    stderr: Error: cannot apply '0' migration files
228	    exit: 1
229	
230	    $ atlas migrate apply -u sqlite://d.db -1
231	    stderr: Error: unknown shorthand flag: '1' in -1
232	    exit: 1        # negative numbers are parsed as flags

330	## 10. Community-edition notices (important, stateful)
331	
332	This build prints community-edition notices to **stderr**. They are rate-limited via
333	state files in `$HOME/.atlas/`, so they appear on the FIRST run with a fresh `$HOME`
334	and then go quiet. All notices respect `NO_COLOR` (see §11).
335	
336	### 10a. Success-path notice (476 bytes, ends with a blank line)
337	
338	Printed on successful runs of commands that connect through the schema/sqlclient
339	path — observed on `schema inspect` and `schema diff` (exit 0). NOT printed by
340	`version`, `license`, `completion *`, `--help` anywhere, `schema fmt`, `migrate status`,
341	`migrate apply`, `migrate validate`, `migrate new`, `migrate lint`.
342	
343	Verbatim (note the trailing space after `views, ` on line 2, the tab-indented
344	command/URL lines, and the final blank line):
345	
346	```
347	Notice: This Atlas edition lacks support for features such as checkpoints,
348	testing, down migrations, and more. Additionally, advanced database objects such as views, 
349	triggers, and stored procedures are not supported. To read more: https://atlasgo.io/community-edition
350	
351	To install the non-community version of Atlas, use the following command:
352	
353		curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh
354	
355	Or, visit the website to see all installation options:
356	
357		https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
358	
359	```
360	
361	Rate limiting: on first show it writes `$HOME/.atlas/local-community.json` containing
362	`{"v1.us":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. The notice is suppressed until the timestamp is
363	more than **7 days** old (empirically: suppressed at age 600000 s, shown at 604800 s).
364	
365	### 10b. Error-path notice (appended to stderr after the `Error:` line)
366	
367	Fires on virtually every error path — flag parse errors, required-flag violations,
368	unknown root commands, connection errors, config errors, runtime errors. The error
369	line comes first, then the notice immediately (no blank line between):
370	
371	    $ atlas schema inspect          # fresh $HOME
372	    stderr:
373	    Error: required flag(s) "url" not set
374	    You're running the community build of Atlas, which may differ from the official version.
375	    If this error persists, try installing the official version as a troubleshooting step:
376	
377	      curl -sSf https://atlasgo.sh | sh
378	
379	    More installation options: https://atlasgo.io/docs#installation
380	    exit: 1
381	
382	(The `curl` line is indented with two spaces; the notice ends with a single `\n`,
383	no trailing blank line.)
384	
385	Rate limiting: writes `$HOME/.atlas/community_error.json` containing
386	`{"last_suggested":"<RFC3339Nano timestamp>"}`. Re-shown only when the timestamp is
387	more than **24 hours** old (suppressed at 82800 s, shown at 86400 s).
388	
389	The two notices are independent (separate files); a success run does not suppress
390	the error notice and vice versa.
391	
392	### 10c. `ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`
393	
394	`ATLAS_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` has **no observable effect** in this build: with a fresh
395	`$HOME`, both the success notice and the error notice are still printed, and the state
396	files are still written. (Earlier runs in a warmed `$HOME` may misleadingly suggest it
397	suppresses the success notice — that is the 7-day rate limit, not the env var.)
398	
399	### 10d. Interplay with output
400	
401	- Notices go to stderr only; stdout is byte-identical whether or not a notice fires.
402	- With a warmed `$HOME` (state files present and fresh), stderr is completely empty
403	  on success paths and contains only the `Error:` line on error paths.

1	# `atlas schema fmt` — Behavioral Spec
2	
3	Binary probed: `/tmp/atlas_orig` (atlas community edition, unofficial dev build).
4	All probes run with stdout/stderr separated (`cmd >out 2>err; echo $?`), piped (non-TTY) unless noted.
5	Probe scratch dir: `/tmp/probe`. Probing user was `root`.
6	
7	## Summary of behavior
8	
9	- Rewrites files **in place**; never prints formatted content to stdout.
10	- Prints to **stdout** the path of each file it actually changed, one per line (path exactly as constructed from the argument, see "Path echoing"). Files already in canonical form produce no output and are **not rewritten** (mtime untouched).
11	- Exit code `0` on success (even for malformed HCL); exit code `1` with `Error: ...` on stderr for stat/flag errors.
12	- Formatting style is canonical `hclwrite.Format` (hashicorp/hcl/v2): token-based, tolerant of syntax errors, preserves comments, heredocs, line-ending style (CRLF kept), and does not add a missing trailing newline.
13	- With no path args, formats `.hcl` files in the **current directory** (non-recursive). Directory args are also **non-recursive**.
14	- Only files whose name ends in lowercase `.hcl` are considered. `.HCL`, `.txt`, extensionless files are silently skipped — even when passed explicitly as arguments.
15	- Hidden files (`*.hcl` dotfiles) **are** processed.
16	- Symlinks to `.hcl` files are followed; the target is rewritten, the link name is printed.
17	- Global flags (`-c/--config`, `--env`, `--var`) are accepted but have no observable effect; no `atlas.hcl` config file is required or consulted.

204	## Formatting semantics (canonical hclwrite style)
205	
206	Observed on a synthetic file covering comments, alignment, lists, function calls, heredocs.
207	
208	Input:
209	
210	```
211	# leading comment
212	// another comment style
213	schema "test" { # inline comment on block
214	  charset = "utf8mb4" # inline attr comment
215	  x   =   1
216	  longer_name = 2
217	  list = [1,  2,    3]
218	  nested_list = [
219	    "a",
220	    "b",
221	  ]
222	  val = func("a",  1 , true)
223	  heredoc = <<EOT
224	  hello   world
225	  indented   more
226	EOT
227	  after = "kept"
228	}
229	/* block
230	   comment */
231	block   "a"   "b"   {
232	  /* inline block comment */ y = 1
233	}
234	```
235	
236	Output (exit 0, filename printed):
237	
238	```
239	# leading comment
240	// another comment style
241	schema "test" {           # inline comment on block
242	  charset     = "utf8mb4" # inline attr comment
243	  x           = 1
244	  longer_name = 2
245	  list        = [1, 2, 3]
246	  nested_list = [
247	    "a",
248	    "b",
249	  ]
250	  val     = func("a", 1, true)
251	  heredoc = <<EOT
252	  hello   world
253	  indented   more
254	EOT
255	  after   = "kept"
256	}
257	/* block
258	   comment */
259	block "a" "b" {
260	  /* inline block comment */ y = 1
261	}
262	```
263	
264	Rules observed:
265	
266	- Multiple spaces between block name/labels/`{` collapse to one: `block   "a"   "b"   {` → `block "a" "b" {`.
267	- `=` of consecutive attributes in the same group are aligned (padded) to the longest name; alignment groups are broken by heredocs, comments-with-content lines behave per hclwrite rules.
268	- Trailing inline comments on consecutive lines are column-aligned (`# inline comment on block` padded to align with `# inline attr comment`).
269	- Spaces around `=` normalized to exactly one each side (plus alignment padding).
270	- Lists: `[1,  2,    3]` → `[1, 2, 3]`; multi-line list layout preserved (one item per line kept).
271	- Function calls: `func("a",  1 , true)` → `func("a", 1, true)`.
272	- Heredocs: marker and **body preserved verbatim** (inner spacing untouched); heredoc breaks the `=` alignment group.
273	- Comments (`#`, `//`, `/* */`) preserved, including block comments spanning lines; standalone comment lines not re-indented beyond their column.
274	- Blank lines preserved, including multiple trailing blank lines at EOF (a file `x = 1\n\n\n\n` is considered already formatted — not listed, not rewritten).
275	
276	### Line endings and EOF newline
277	
278	- **CRLF preserved**: input `x = 1\r\ny    =    2\r\n` → output `x = 1\r\ny = 2\r\n` (spacing fixed, `\r\n` kept).
279	- **No trailing newline added**: file containing exactly `x = 1` (no `\n`) is considered already formatted — not listed, not rewritten.
280	
281	## File metadata / write behavior
282	
283	- Already-formatted files are **not rewritten**: mtime unchanged after running fmt on them (verified with `stat -c %Y` before/after).
284	- Rewritten files **keep their permission bits** (640 stayed 640).
285	- Read-only file (mode 444) was still formatted successfully — but the probe ran as `root`, so this may fail for unprivileged users; reimplementation should expect a write error to surface as `Error: ...` on stderr with exit 1 (not directly observed).
286	- Symlink arg (`link.hcl` → `linktarget.hcl`): target rewritten in place, stdout printed the **link name** `link.hcl`, exit 0.
287	
288	## TTY vs piped
289	
290	Command under pseudo-TTY: `script -qec '/tmp/atlas_orig schema fmt ttydir/t.hcl' /dev/null`
291	Exit code: `0`. Output identical to piped mode except line endings appear as `\r\n` (pty driver artifact): `ttydir/t.hcl\r\n`. No prompts, spinners, colors, or other TTY-dependent behavior.
292	
293	## Global flags
294	
295	`atlas schema fmt --env foo withfiles` → exit 0, normal behavior. No `atlas.hcl` was present in any probe directory; fmt never complained about a missing config file. `-c/--config`, `--var` were not observed to alter behavior.
296	
297	## Reimplementation checklist
298	
299	1. Args: zero or more paths; default `["."]`.
300	2. For each arg in order: `os.Stat`; on failure print `Error: stat <arg>: no such file or directory` (Go `os.Stat` error text) to stderr, exit 1, stop processing further args.
301	3. If arg is a dir: list entries (alphabetical), take only regular entries ending in `.hcl` (lowercase), non-recursive, dotfiles included; join paths with `filepath.Join` semantics (`.` → bare name).
302	4. If arg is a file: process only if name ends in `.hcl`; else skip silently.
303	5. For each candidate: read bytes, run `hclwrite.Format`, compare; if different, write back (preserving mode) and print the path + `\n` to stdout.
304	6. Unknown flags: `Error: unknown flag: --<name>` on stderr, exit 1, no usage text.
305	7. Exit 0 otherwise. Never print formatted content; never read stdin.

190	## 3. Approval prompt (default, no `--dry-run`/`--auto-approve`)
191	
192	After printing the plan to stdout, an interactive select prompt is shown **even when
193	stdin/stdout are not TTYs** (ANSI escape sequences are emitted unconditionally).
194	Prompt is part of stdout; nothing on stderr unless an error occurs.
195	
196	Initial frame (rendered via `cat -v`):
197	
198	```
199	^[[?25l^[[2K^M^[[34m?^[[0m Are you sure?: 
200	^[[2K^M  ^[[1mM-bM-^VM-8^[[0m ^[[4mApply^[[0m
201	^[[2K^M    Abort
202	```
203	
204	i.e. hide-cursor `ESC[?25l`, then a blue `?` (`ESC[34m?ESC[0m`), the literal text
205	` Are you sure?: `, then two option lines: `▸ Apply` (bold `▸` = `ESC[1m…ESC[0m`,
206	underlined `Apply` = `ESC[4m…ESC[0m`) and `    Abort`. The default selection is **Apply**.
207	
208	Behavior by input:
209	
210	- **EOF on stdin** (e.g. `</dev/null` or an immediately-closed pipe): prompt is
211	  aborted. stdout ends with cursor-restore `ESC[?25h`; stderr gets exactly:
212	
213	  ```
214	  Error: ^D
215	  ```
216	
217	  Exit code `1`. Nothing is applied. (The literal text is caret-D, not a control byte.)
218	- **Newline** (`echo "" | …`) or **`y\n`** (`echo "y" | …` — the `y` is ignored, the
219	  newline selects): selects the highlighted option (Apply). Final frame redraws the
220	  selection as a green check + dim label:
221	  `ESC[32mESC[32m✔ESC[0m ESC[2mApplyESC[0m\n` then `ESC[?25h`. Exit `0`, changes applied.
222	- **Arrow-down then Enter** (`printf '\x1b[B\n' | …`) or **`j` then Enter**
223	  (`printf 'j\n' | …`): moves highlight to Abort and confirms it. Final frame shows
224	  `✔ Abort`. **Exit `0`, no error message, nothing applied** — user abort is a clean
225	  success exit.
226	- Extra positional args are silently ignored: `atlas schema apply extra-arg -u … --to …`
227	  behaves exactly as without `extra-arg` (plan + prompt).
228	- Under a pseudo-TTY (`script -qec '…' /dev/null </dev/null`), the same frames are
229	  produced with CRLF endings; with EOF the `Error: ^D` line lands on the terminal
230	  (stdout+stderr merged by the pty). Overall behavior is identical to non-TTY — there
231	  is no TTY gating of the prompt.
232	
233	Successful apply (approved or `--auto-approve`) prints **nothing after the plan** in
234	the default format — no "applied N statements" summary.

95	## 3. `--auto-approve` (happy path)
96	
97	Command: `/tmp/atlas_orig schema clean -u "sqlite://t2.db" --auto-approve >out 2>err`
98	
99	Exit code: `0`. stderr empty. **stdout** exactly (trailing newline after last line, no extra output — no "applied" confirmation):
100	
101	```text
102	-- Planned Changes:
103	-- Disable the enforcement of foreign-keys constraints
104	PRAGMA foreign_keys = off;
105	-- Drop "users" table
106	DROP TABLE `users`;
107	-- Drop "posts" table
108	DROP TABLE `posts`;
109	-- Enable back the enforcement of foreign-keys constraints
110	PRAGMA foreign_keys = on;
111	```
112	
113	Post-run database contents (`SELECT type, name FROM sqlite_master`):
114	
115	```text
116	[('view', 'user_names')]
117	```
118	
119	**Important:** on SQLite, `schema clean` (community edition) drops **tables only**:
120	
121	- The plan contains one `DROP TABLE` per table, wrapped in `PRAGMA foreign_keys = off;` / `PRAGMA foreign_keys = on;` with the exact comment lines shown above.
122	- **Views are never dropped** and never appear in the plan. `user_names` survives the clean.
123	- Indexes and triggers are not dropped explicitly; they disappear implicitly with their tables.
124	- Drop order follows `sqlite_master` insertion (creation) order, NOT alphabetical: for tables created as `zebra, apple, mango` the plan drops `zebra`, then `apple`, then `mango` (verified separately).
125	- Object names in comments use double quotes (`-- Drop "users" table`); SQL identifiers use backticks (``DROP TABLE `users`;``).
126	- Running clean a second time on the same DB (now containing only the view) prints `Nothing to drop` (see §6).
