324	## 9. Summary of behavioral rules (for reimplementation)
325	
326	1. `-u/--url` is required; missing → `Error: required flag(s) "url" not set`, exit 1, stderr only.
327	2. `--dry-run` and `--format` are gated in the community build: `Abort: 'atlas schema clean --<flag>' is not supported by the community version.` + install block, exit 1, stderr only, before any DB work.
328	3. With zero tables: print `Nothing to drop` to stdout, exit 0, never prompt.
329	4. With tables: print the plan to stdout:
330	   - header `-- Planned Changes:`
331	   - `-- Disable the enforcement of foreign-keys constraints` / `PRAGMA foreign_keys = off;`
332	   - per table (in `sqlite_master` creation order): `-- Drop "<name>" table` + ``DROP TABLE `<name>`;``
333	   - `-- Enable back the enforcement of foreign-keys constraints` / `PRAGMA foreign_keys = on;`
334	5. SQLite community clean drops **tables only**; views survive; indexes/triggers vanish implicitly with their tables.
335	6. Without `--auto-approve`, show an interactive select prompt on stdout (even when piped): `? Are you sure?: ` with options `Apply` (default) / `Abort`.
336	   - Apply → execute plan, exit 0, no further message.
337	   - Abort → execute nothing, exit 0, no message.
338	   - EOF on stdin → `Error: ^D` on stderr, exit 1.
339	   - First SIGINT → stdout warning `interrupt received, wait for exit or ^C to terminate`, keeps waiting; second SIGINT → exit 1, stderr `Error: ^D`, nothing dropped.
340	7. With `--auto-approve`: plan printed, executed immediately, exit 0, no prompt, no confirmation message.
341	8. Connecting to a nonexistent sqlite file in an existing directory creates the empty file as a side effect.
342	9. Extra positional arguments are ignored.

115	## 2. `atlas migrate new [name]`
116	
117	### Happy path
118	
119	- Default `--dir` is `file://migrations` (relative to CWD). If the directory does not exist it is **created silently** (mode 0755).
120	- Creates one empty file (0 bytes, mode 0644) named:
121	  - no name given: `<timestamp>.sql`, e.g. `20260810055924.sql`
122	  - with name: `<timestamp>_<name>.sql`, e.g. `20260810060023_myname.sql`
123	- `<timestamp>` = **local time** at run, format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` (14 digits). Verified identical to `date` output on the host.
124	- `<name>` is used **verbatim**: spaces and capitals preserved (`20260810061016_with space and CAPS.sql`).
125	- After creating the file it **(re-)writes `atlas.sum`** in the same directory (silent).
126	- Success output: **completely silent** (stdout and stderr empty), exit 0.
127	- Two runs in the same second with different names produce distinct files sharing the same timestamp prefix.
128	- Two runs in the same second with the **same** name: exit 0, silent — the same filename is reused (file simply re-created empty).
129	- `--edit` with `EDITOR=true`: exit 0, silent (opens `$EDITOR` on the new file).
130	- `--dir file:///abs/path` (absolute file URL) works, creates dir if needed.
131	
132	### `migrate new` validates the directory first
133	
134	If the existing directory fails checksum validation, `new` aborts **without creating a file**, printing the same checksum report as `validate` (see §5), exit 1.
135	
136	### `migrate new` error cases
137	
138	Two positional args:
139

143	--err--
144	Error: accepts at most 1 arg(s), received 2
145	exit=1
146	```
147	
148	Unknown flag (no usage text printed):
149

151	$ atlas migrate new --badflag
152	--err--
153	Error: unknown flag: --badflag
154	exit=1
155	```
156	
157	Name containing `/` (treated as path separator; parent dir missing):
158	
159	```
160	$ atlas migrate new "a/b"
161	--err--
162	Error: open migrations/20260810060953_a/b.sql: no such file or directory
163	exit=1
164	```
165	
166	`--dir` without URL scheme (note: trailing space before the newline is exact):
167	
168	```
169	$ atlas migrate new --dir migrations q
170	--out-- (empty)
171	--err-- (od -c verified: ends with `?` SPACE `\n`)
172	Error: missing scheme for dir url. Did you mean "file://migrations"? 
173	exit=1
174	```
175	
176	Unknown `--dir-format`:
177

185	### `--dir-format` naming and file templates
186	
187	All formats still use the same timestamp. Formats other than `atlas` may create **two** files and/or pre-fill template content. Verified in fresh empty dirs (timestamp `20260810061222`, name `gm`/`fy`; `test_<fmt>` otherwise):
188	
189	| `--dir-format` | Files created | File content |
190	|---|---|---|
191	| `atlas` (default) | `20260810061016_<name>.sql` | empty (0 bytes) |
192	| `goose` | `20260810061016_<name>.sql` | `-- +goose Up\n\n-- +goose Down\n` (29 bytes) |
193	| `dbmate` | `20260810061017_<name>.sql` | `-- migrate:up\n\n-- migrate:down\n` (31 bytes) |
194	| `liquibase` | `20260810061017_<name>.sql` | `--liquibase formatted sql` (25 bytes, **no trailing newline**) |
195	| `golang-migrate` | `20260810061222_<name>.up.sql` **and** `20260810061222_<name>.down.sql` | both empty |
196	| `flyway` | `V20260810061222__<name>.sql` **and** `U20260810061222__<name>.sql` (double underscore) | both empty |
197	
198	Note: with non-atlas formats, only the "up" migration file is tracked in `atlas.sum` (golang-migrate: only `*.up.sql`; flyway: only `V*.sql` — see §4). Also, running `new --dir-format golang-migrate` (or `flyway`) in a dir that already contains atlas-format `.sql` files + `atlas.sum` fails with the checksum report ("was removed"), because those formats don't match the existing files.

226	## 4. `atlas.sum` format — fully reverse-engineered
227	
228	### Which files are included
229	
230	- Only **regular files directly in the directory** whose name ends with **lowercase `.sql`**.
231	  - Uppercase `.SQL` is excluded.
232	  - Hidden files like `.hidden.sql` **are** included.
233	  - Non-`.sql` files (e.g. `README.txt`) are excluded.
234	  - Subdirectories (and `.sql` files inside them) are excluded.
235	  - `atlas.sum` itself is excluded.
236	- Files are processed in **byte-wise lexicographic name order** (Go `sort.Strings`): e.g. `.hidden.sql` < `20240101000000_a.sql`, `A1.sql` < `Z1.sql` < `b1.sql`.
237	
238	### File layout
239	
240	```
241	h1:<base64(total)>\n
242	<name1> h1:<base64(chainhash1)>\n
243	<name2> h1:<base64(chainhash2)>\n
244	...
245	```
246	
247	- Base64 is standard encoding (`+`, `/`, `=` padding).
248	- Every line, including the last, ends with `\n` when written by the tool.
249	- Single space between name and `h1:`.
250	
251	### The hash algorithm (verified byte-exact against the binary on 8 different directories)
252	
253	Per-file hashes form a **chain** over the sorted files: one running SHA-256 state; for each file, the file **name bytes** then the raw **content bytes** are written into the state; the file's hash is the current digest:
254	
255	```
256	h = sha256()
257	for f in sorted_files:
258	    h.update(f.name_bytes)
259	    h.update(f.content_bytes)     # raw bytes, no normalization; no trailing-newline fixups
260	    filehash[f] = h.digest()      # cumulative!
261	```
262	
263	Consequence: the listed hash of file *i* depends on **all files before it** (names + contents). Adding a file at the front changes every later file's hash. E.g. alone, `20240102000000_add_name.sql` with content `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN name TEXT;` (no trailing newline) hashes to `CPbnUVFtz1pdtaGE9+esbIfu1ML9gSb/YL7uZrCjbVc=`; after prepending another file it becomes `W/ZgPdxVESXKlnwrxgkuUH2NdSjIxhAxzYtLGVnFGDo=`.
264	
265	The total (first line) is a **separate** SHA-256 over the concatenation, in the same file order, of each file's name bytes followed by its base64-encoded chain-hash **string** bytes:
266	
267	```
268	t = sha256()
269	for f in sorted_files:
270	    t.update(f.name_bytes)
271	    t.update(base64encode(filehash[f]))   # the 44-char ASCII base64 string
272	total = t.digest()
273	```
274	
275	### Reference implementation (reproduces the binary's `atlas.sum` byte-for-byte)
276	
277	```python
278	import hashlib, base64, os
279	
280	def atlas_sum(d):
281	    files = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(d)
282	                   if f.endswith(".sql") and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, f)))
283	    chain, total, lines = hashlib.sha256(), hashlib.sha256(), []
284	    for n in files:
285	        chain.update(n.encode())
286	        chain.update(open(os.path.join(d, n), "rb").read())
287	        hb = base64.b64encode(chain.copy().digest()).decode()
288	        lines.append(f"{n} h1:{hb}")
289	        total.update(n.encode())
290	        total.update(hb.encode())
291	    return ("h1:" + base64.b64encode(total.digest()).decode() + "\n"
292	            + "".join(l + "\n" for l in lines)).encode()
293	```

1	# Spec: `atlas schema diff` (community dev build, binary `/tmp/atlas_orig`)

4	captured non-TTY (piped) unless noted. `stdout` and `stderr` are always reported separately.

6	## General behavior
7	
8	- `atlas schema diff --from <url> --to <url> [--dev-url <url>]` prints a SQL migration plan
9	  that transforms the `--from` schema into the `--to` schema.
10	- Both `-f`/`--from` and `--to` are **required** flags (repeatable `strings`).
11	- The plan is printed to **stdout**; every statement is preceded by a `-- comment` line.
12	  Each line (comments and statements) ends with a single `\n`; the final statement ends
13	  with exactly one trailing `\n`. No blank lines anywhere in the output.
14	- Exit code is `0` on success (including "no changes"), `1` on any error.
15	  Errors go to **stderr** as `Error: <message>\n` with empty stdout.
16	- Identical schemas print to **stdout** (exit 0):
17	  ```
18	  Schemas are synced, no changes to be made.
19	  ```
20	- Non-TTY vs TTY: output bytes are identical apart from the pty's `\n`→`\r\n` translation.
21	  **No ANSI color codes**, no spinners, no prompts in either mode (verified via
22	  `script -qec ... /dev/null`, zero `0x1b` bytes).
23	- `--dev-url` is required whenever a `file://` (HCL) URL is used in `--from` or `--to`;
24	  it is accepted but ignored when both sides are database URLs.
25	  `sqlite://dev?mode=memory` works as dev-url.
26	- HCL↔HCL diffs produce byte-identical SQL to the equivalent sqlite↔sqlite diff
27	  (HCL is normalized through the dev database).
28	- A nonexistent sqlite file in an existing directory is **created** (0 bytes) and treated
29	  as an empty schema; diff succeeds.
